densityModes.name: scale: mobile (large)
densityModes.description: Touch devices: sizes and font sizes are about 1.25× desktop.

controls.note: T-shirt sizes XS–XL map to component-height-50/75/100/200/300.

structure.note: Ramps (gray 25–1000, hues 100–1600) each with light/dark/wireframe values → semantic palette (accent, informative, negative, notice, positive → a hue ramp; accent = blue) → aliases.

findings: Spectrum is the only system here with script-specific line-height tokens: cjk-line-height-100 = 1.5 against line-height-100 = 1.3, and cjk-line-height-200 = 1.7 against line-height-200 = 1.5; plus cjk-font-family (Adobe Clean Han) and cjk-letter-spacing. The precedent — a script gets its own multiplier token — is exactly what Arabic needs, but no Arabic, Hebrew or RTL token exists.

Component text uses fixed px line heights tied to each font size (line-height-font-size-100 = 18px for 14px on desktop, 22px for 17px on mobile), ratio ≈ 1.29, with no CJK or other script variant for components.

Platform scale is a first-class dimension: every size token has desktop and mobile values (component-height-100 32px → 40px, font-size-100 14px → 17px): touch gets ×1.25 on height and a larger font, not just padding.
Density words appear only on a few layout tokens (117 names containing compact/spacious: list gaps, group gaps, field icon offsets), not as a global mode.
Direction: tokens use logical names (text-align-start/end, field-end-edge-…, edge-to-text); there is no direction token.

gaps: No motion (duration/easing), breakpoint, container or z-index tokens in this package.
No touch-target minimum token; touch is handled by the mobile scale.
Font weights are named (regular, medium, bold…), not numeric.
